ddl:
CREATE TABLE User (
    Last_Login_Time DATETIME,
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Registration_Time DATETIME,
    Role VARCHAR(255),
    User_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Username VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Article (
    Article_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Author VARCHAR(255),
    Content VARCHAR(255),
    Publish_Time DATETIME,
    Title VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Book (
    Author VARCHAR(255),
    Book_Description VARCHAR(255),
    Book_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Title VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Activity (
    Activity_Description VARCHAR(255),
    Activity_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Activity_Name VARCHAR(255),
    Activity_Time DATETIME
);

CREATE TABLE Video_Interview (
    Publish_Time DATETIME,
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    Video_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Video_Link VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE User_Comments (
    Article_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Comment_Content VARCHAR(255),
    Comment_Time DATETIME,
    User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (User_ID, Article_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Article_ID) REFERENCES Article(Article_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Book_Recommendation (
    Book_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Book_Review VARCHAR(255),
    Recommendation_Reason VARCHAR(255),
    Recommendation_Time DATETIME,
    Recommender_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Book_ID, Recommender_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Book_ID) REFERENCES Book(Book_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Recommender_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Activity_Lottery (
    Activity_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Prize_Name VARCHAR(255),
    Winner_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Activity_ID, Winner_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Activity_ID) REFERENCES Activity(Activity_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Winner_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE User_Activity_Participation (
    Activity_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Participation_Time DATETIME,
    User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (User_ID, Activity_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Activity_ID) REFERENCES Activity(Activity_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);
gold_question:
The system is a user-article sharing forum with the following features:
1.User Interaction Features:
Each user has a unique User ID, Username, Password, Registration Time, Last Login Time, and Role.
A user can participate in multiple activities, engage in video interviews, and comment or recommend books and articles.
2.Content Management:
The system manages several books and articles.
Book Information: Each book has a Book ID, Title, Author, and Description.
Article Information: Each article has an Article ID, Title, Content, Author, and Publish Time.
Activity Information: Each activity has an Activity ID, Activity Name, Activity Time, and Description.
Video Interview Information: Each video interview has a Video ID, Title, Video Link, and Publish Time.
3.Activity Management:
The system can organize source code reading activities, record activity names, times, and descriptions.
Users can participate in multiple activities.
The system also handles lottery activities, recording winner information and awarding gifts.

The database schema named 'rschema_0248' contains 9 tables. The tables are User, Article, Book, Activity, Video_Interview, User_Comments, Book_Recommendation, Activity_Lottery, and User_Activity_Participation.
The User table represents a user of the system and contains columns for the user's last login time, password, registration time, role, user ID, and username. All columns allow null values. The User_ID is the primary key.
The Article table represents an article in the system and contains columns for the article's ID, author, content, publish time, and title. All columns allow null values. The Article_ID is the primary key.
The Book table represents a book in the system and contains columns for the book's author, description, ID, and title. All columns allow null values. The Book_ID is the primary key.
The Activity table represents an activity in the system and contains columns for the activity's description, ID, name, and time. All columns allow null values. The Activity_ID is the primary key.
The Video_Interview table represents a video interview in the system and contains columns for the publish time, title, and video link. All columns allow null values. The Video_ID is the primary key.
The User_Comments table represents user comments on articles and contains columns for the article ID, comment content, comment time, and user ID. The User_ID and Article_ID are foreign keys referencing the User and Article tables respectively.
The Book_Recommendation table represents book recommendations and contains columns for the book ID, review, recommendation reason, recommendation time, and recommender ID. The Book_ID and Recommender_ID are foreign keys referencing the Book and User tables respectively.
The Activity_Lottery table represents activity lotteries and contains columns for the activity ID, prize name, and winner ID. The Activity_ID and Winner_ID are foreign keys referencing the Activity and User tables respectively.
The User_Activity_Participation table represents user activity participations and contains columns for the activity ID, participation time, and user ID. The User_ID and Activity_ID are foreign keys referencing the User and Activity tables respectively.
This schema ensures referential integrity by enforcing foreign key constraints. It also ensures entity integrity by ensuring that each table has a primary key and that primary keys are unique and not null. It also ensures domain integrity by ensuring that the data types of the columns match the expected data type.
